current_example.problem: Find the principal axes of the curve $19x_1^2-6x_1x_2+11x_2^2 = 20.$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, consider the quadratic form $Q(\mathbf{x})=19x_1^2-6x_1x_2+11x_2^2.$ The matrix of the form is 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/f817e7083774590c64b100e995c3a54127aa160b763816471412200f38d7c26f.svg)

Notice that $A$ is symmetric. The principal axes of the curve 

$$
\mathbf{x}^T \! A \mathbf{x} = 20
$$

are the vectors that form an orthonormal eigenvector basis of $A.$ 

By solving the characteristic equation $|A-\lambda I| = 0,$ we obtain

$\qquad$ $\lambda_1=20 \quad$ and $\quad \lambda_2=10.$

Let's now find the eigenvectors.

- For $\lambda_2=20,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-20I & =[\begin{aligned}19 & -3 \\ -3 & 11\end{aligned}]-20[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ -3 & -9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-20I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/f2a97981a1e61c3aa9e04427abe4128c3a18a753975af8d370f14f1d07f6ffbf.svg) Dividing $\mathbf{v}_2$ by its norm $\| \mathbf{v}_2  \| = \sqrt{10},$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/f824ac150d66c196a167f8ff98ace9ef54429e99c4228f879f829b1c134f292f.svg)

- For $\lambda_1=10,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-10I & =[\begin{aligned}19 & -3 \\ -3 & 11\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-10I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/f68f79da87f8b7fe0e7e4a1f55c9ee629c1256f448221187ebbbd4df25b06758.svg) Dividing $\mathbf{v}_1$ by its norm $\| \mathbf{v}_1  \| = \sqrt{10},$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/cb6b9a7c601b3621cb532732b47bdcf97f9a23202d9176027f7f1d3c27f7a437.svg)

Therefore, the principal axes of our curve are

$\qquad$ ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/71afe57916b7ed211b9d34e1f22bd9fb0d8e89b5ee3079e4b8aa44b6aa9c5e13.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/625711fd761e03ed7facabaf58bf2f4f416571e4c19d82617cada29901808b2b.svg)
